claims.statement: `Institution.csv_format` on `account_institutions` is a comma-separated positional template string mapping each column of a broker CSV export to a standardized placeholder, and it is the only per-broker configuration the generic parser consumes — there is no broker-specific branching in `src/account/csv/parser.py`.

`normalize_token` is the single normalization rule applied to both template tokens and file headers — it strips a leading UTF-8 BOM and whitespace, unwraps `{...}`, lowercases, and collapses non-alphanumeric runs into single underscores — so real-world broker labels only match the template through the `HEADER_ALIASES` table.

`header_matches` accepts a header alias match in either direction (actual in `HEADER_ALIASES[expected]` or expected in `HEADER_ALIASES[actual]`), which is what lets a `{type}` template token line up with a file column labeled `Security Type`.

Header validation is two-stage and strictly positional: a raw column-count mismatch raises `CsvHeaderCountMismatchError` before any name comparison, and the first element-wise name mismatch raises `CsvHeaderColumnMismatchError` with a 1-based column index; a reordered export therefore fails even when every label is recognized.

`map_account_type` lowercases and trims the raw account type and resolves only the documented `ACCOUNT_TYPE_MAP` keys (TFSA/RRSP/FHSA variants plus non-registered/personal/margin) to `AccountTypeEnum`; an unrecognized value raises `CsvUnsupportedAccountTypeError` and aborts the entire parse rather than skipping the row.

`_parse_position` treats quantity and book value asymmetrically: an unparseable quantity raises `CsvInvalidQuantityError` (and a missing quantity cell silently parses as `Decimal("0")`), while an unparseable book value is swallowed into `None` so a malformed cost basis degrades to unknown cost instead of failing the import.

`calculate_average_cost` returns `None` for non-positive quantity or missing book value, otherwise quantizes `book_value / quantity` to 4 decimal places with `ROUND_HALF_UP`; that quantize step fixes every CSV-imported `average_cost` and cascades into all downstream cost-basis P&L.

GenericCsvParser.parse rejects blank content with CsvEmptyError and strips a leading BOM, then enforces per-row invariants while grouping by account_number: every row needs a non-empty account number (CsvMissingAccountNumberError(row_idx)), but only the first row seen for a new account number needs a non-empty account type (CsvMissingAccountTypeError(row_idx)) — the account type is mapped and the account currency resolved at that first sighting. Accounts are returned in first-seen order with row_idx reported as a 1-based file line number starting at 2, and each CsvDiscoveredAccount carries free_cash rounded to 2 dp plus the exists flag defaulting to False.

Row classification runs before the quantity parse in `_parse_position`, so a filtered row can never raise CsvInvalidQuantityError, but the two filters behave differently: cash rows (per `is_cash_row`) are consumed — `_parse_cash_amount` adds the first parseable of quantity, market_value, book_value, book_value_cad or book_value_market into the account's free_cash accumulator — while option rows (`is_option_row`: security_type containing option/derivative, or an OCC-pattern symbol) are skipped with no contribution. `is_cash_row` short-circuits to False for security_type values exchange_traded_fund/etf/equity/stock/mutual_fund so a listed ETF literally named `CASH` stays a position. Options are defended a second time in `sync_account_csv_positions` via `is_option_symbol`.

The parser's exception taxonomy is rooted at `CsvParserError` with three branches — `CsvHeaderValidationError` (count/column), `CsvEmptyError` (empty content, empty template, no columns; plus the service-level `CsvFileEmptyError` subclass), and `CsvRowValidationError` (unsupported account type, missing account number, missing account type, invalid quantity) — and the router maps `CsvParserError` to HTTP 400 with the message as `detail`.

All three CSV endpoints (`POST /accounts/csv/inspect`, `/accounts/csv/import`, `/accounts/{account_id}/csv-sync`) share one gate: `CsvAccountService.validate_csv_institution` raises `InstitutionNotFoundError` (404) when the institution row is missing and `CsvImportDisabledError` (400) when `csv_import_enabled` is false OR `csv_format` is empty, so `csv_import_enabled=True` with `csv_format=None` behaves identically to a disabled institution.

`inspect_csv` validates the institution, rejects blank content with `CsvFileEmptyError` before parsing, then when a `user_id` is given it marks `exists = True` and overwrites each discovered account's currency with the stored `Account.currency` for account numbers the user already has at that institution; `exists` drives the modal's `Update holdings` versus `Create account` badge.

`import_accounts` filters parsed accounts against the requested `account_numbers` and raises `NoMatchingAccountsInCsvError` when the intersection is empty — there is no import-everything mode. `CsvAccountDuplicateError` is mapped to 400 by the router but is never raised on this path: a requested number that already exists is treated as an in-place update returning the same account id.

Accounts created by CSV import are stamped `api_sync_enabled=False` and `integration_user_id=None`, which is what makes the broker sync path refuse them (`POST /{account_id}/sync` returns 400 and `PositionService.sync_account_positions` raises `ApiSyncDisabledError`) and makes the frontend account-row refresh control render `Update from CSV` instead of `Sync positions`, opening the CSV update modal instead of calling `onSync`.

Currency resolution at import has a defined precedence per account: the caller-supplied `account_currencies[number]` (trimmed and uppercased) wins, then the parsed account currency, then `"CAD"`; for an existing account a difference triggers `AccountRepository.update_currency` (which raises `ValueError` for a missing row), and for a new account it becomes the `AccountSchema.currency`.

`sync_account_from_csv` is asymmetric with import: it never creates an account, never changes the account currency, and never considers other discovered accounts in the file — it matches only the target account's `external_id` (raising `AccountNotInCsvError` otherwise), updates only `free_cash` and positions, validates the account's own institution's CSV enablement, and is the only CSV endpoint that enforces account ownership (404 for another user's account). It accepts either an `AccountSchema` or an `AccountId`, resolving the latter through the repository and raising `AccountNotFoundError` when missing.

`sync_account_csv_positions` is the shared tail for all three paths: it resolves each symbol through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` (wrapping a `ValueError` from the market layer as `SecurityResolutionError`, which the router maps to 400), then writes via `PositionApi.create` — which replaces every position row for the account — or calls `sync_by_account(account_id, [])` when the resolved list is empty, so an all-cash export clears the account instead of leaving stale rows; finally it stamps `update_last_sync_at`.

Security resolution for CSV positions is institution-scoped and cached through `SecurityBroker` rows: a repeat `(institution, broker_symbol, broker_exchange)` short-circuits to the mapped security, and a new pair maps the broker symbol/exchange to an EODHD query (`TSX`→`TO`, `CSE`→`CA`, `NYSE`/`NASDAQ`→`US`, `.`→`-`), searches the cached gateway, creates or reuses the security, primes its latest close, and records the raw search results.

The CSV endpoints accept `institution_id`, `account_numbers` and `currencies` as either multipart form fields or query parameters with the same alias (form wins); `institution_id` and `account_numbers` are mandatory (422), account numbers accept a JSON list string, a comma-separated string, or repeated values and are deduplicated in order, and a malformed `currencies` JSON is silently ignored rather than rejected.
None of the three CSV endpoints carries a rate limit — only `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` is decorated with `@limiter.limit("3/minute")` in `src/account/router.py`.

All three CSV endpoints decode the upload with `content_bytes.decode("utf-8-sig")`, so a UTF-8 BOM never reaches the parser and a read/decode failure produces an HTTP 400 rather than an unhandled 500; the parser additionally strips a leading BOM defensively.

`WEALTHSIMPLE_CSV_FORMAT` in `src/commands/seed.py` is the worked example of the template contract: 21 placeholders in Wealthsimple column order, seeded onto the `WEALTHSIMPLE` institution with `csv_import_enabled=True` and re-asserted on every seed run for an already-existing institution, so a template change reaches an existing database.

Onboarding a new broker CSV export is a data change, not a code change: set `csv_format` to the positional template matching the export header and `csv_import_enabled = True`; parser code only needs touching when the export requires placeholder vocabulary the parser does not consume or a header label no alias covers. The caveat is that templates omitting `{account_number}` or `{account_type}` fail at runtime with the row-level missing errors, and omitting `{quantity}` silently yields zero-quantity positions. Both flags are plain `InstitutionModel` columns introduced by the Alembic revision that also adds `accounts.api_sync_enabled`.

The institution seam surfaces to the frontend through `GET /integration/institutions`, which returns `csv_import_enabled` and `csv_format`; the import modal filters that list to `csv_import_enabled === true` and auto-selects the broker when exactly one remains, so adding a second CSV broker requires no frontend change.

`import-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a two-step dialog (broker+file, then a preview table) with client-side `.csv`-extension and 10 MB size guards that disable the primary button, an empty-account-list error that keeps the user on step 1, all discovered accounts selected by default with select-all/indeterminate header state, per-row currency dropdowns, and `Back` preserving the broker and file.

`AccountClient.importAccountsCsv`'s fourth parameter is overloaded as `currenciesOrToken?: Record<string,string> | string | null`: a string is routed to the auth token while an object becomes the stringified `currencies` form field, and the client sends repeated `account_numbers` fields.

Both CSV modals render the backend `detail` string verbatim in a destructive alert, so the parser's diagnostic messages (column index, expected and actual header names, row index, symbol, account type) are what end users actually read.

Focused CSV coverage is layered: `tests/account/csv/test_parser.py` pins the template/alias/filter/rounding/free-cash contract, `tests/services/test_csv_account_service.py` pins the institution gate and the create/update/sync branches with mocked repositories and `SecurityApi` (no outbound calls), `tests/routers/test_csv_inspect.py` and `tests/routers/test_csv_account_endpoints.py` drive the real FastAPI app against Postgres asserting status codes and `PositionModel` rows, and `tests/commands/test_seed.py` pins the seeded template plus seed idempotency.

`_parse_template` reads the template with `csv.reader`, keeps only the first non-empty row, drops cells that strip to blank, and raises `CsvTemplateEmptyError` for an empty template or `CsvNoColumnsDefinedError` when the first row yields no tokens; `_validate_headers` then skips blank leading rows (raising `CsvEmptyError` if none), compares raw column counts first (`CsvHeaderCountMismatchError`), and only then compares normalized header names element-wise, raising `CsvHeaderColumnMismatchError` with a 1-based column index.

`header_matches` accepts a match in either direction — the actual header in `HEADER_ALIASES[expected]` or the expected token in `HEADER_ALIASES[actual]` — which is why the shared `type` alias can serve both `account_type` and `security_type`. Because the row-level lookup is a separate `row_dict.get("account_type")` keyed by normalized template token, `{account_type}` must be present in the template for account-type discovery to work at all.

`is_cash_row` first exempts listed instruments (`exchange_traded_fund`, `etf`, `equity`, `stock`, `mutual_fund` after replacing spaces with underscores) so a Wealthsimple ETF whose ticker is `CASH` is parsed as a position, and otherwise flags a row as cash when the symbol is empty, `security_type` is `cash` or `currency`, or the symbol is `cash`/`cad`/`usd` or starts with `sec-c-`. Cash rows are consumed into the account's `free_cash` via `_parse_cash_amount`, which takes the first parseable of quantity, market_value, book_value, book_value_cad, book_value_market after stripping `,` and `$`; `free_cash` is persisted through `update_free_cash` on all three CSV paths.

`sync_account_csv_positions` resolves each non-option `CsvPositionRecord` through `SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` with `pos.exchange or ""` and `pos.name or ""`, wrapping a market-layer `ValueError` as `SecurityResolutionError` (HTTP 400); it then calls `PositionApi.create` for a non-empty list or `PositionRepository.sync_by_account(account_id, [])` for an empty one, and always stamps `update_last_sync_at`. `sync_by_account` deletes every `PositionModel` row for the account before inserting the new set, making a CSV sync a replace-not-merge operation.

`SecurityApi.get_or_create_from_broker` short-circuits on an existing `SecurityBroker` mapping for the institution/symbol/exchange triple; otherwise it maps the broker symbol (`.` → `-`) and exchange (`TSX` → `TO`, `CSE` → `CA`, `NYSE`/`NASDAQ` → `US`), searches a cached query, raises `ValueError("No search results for …")` on zero results, then creates or reuses the security, primes its latest close, and records the `SecurityBroker` row with the raw search results and mapped symbols.

The import and csv-sync handlers share a decode step — `await file.read()` then `.decode("utf-8-sig")`, with any exception mapped to HTTP 400 `"Failed to read or decode CSV file: …"` — and `import_accounts` persists `disc_acc.free_cash` via `update_free_cash` for existing accounts, while `sync_account_from_csv` does the same against the matched discovered account. `CsvAccountService.validate_csv_institution` converts the institution id with `int()` and raises `InstitutionNotFoundError` for a missing row or `CsvImportDisabledError` when `csv_import_enabled` is false or `csv_format` is empty.

`POST /accounts/csv/import` requires `institution_id` and `account_numbers` (422 for either missing, accepting both as form fields or query params aliased to the same names), normalizes repeated `account_numbers` values that may be JSON lists, comma-separated strings or bare values while deduplicating with `dict.fromkeys`, and parses an optional `currencies` JSON object field tolerantly — a `JSONDecodeError` or non-dict payload is ignored and the accepted values are uppercased. None of the three CSV endpoints carries a rate limit, unlike `POST /accounts/{account_id}/sync` at `3/minute`.

The frontend clients and modals keep the CSV flow's addressing minimal: `accountClient` exposes `inspectCsv`, `importAccountsCsv` (whose fourth parameter is overloaded as either the currency map or a token) and `syncAccountCsv`, which posts only the file to `/accounts/{accountId}/csv-sync`; `import-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a two-step broker-then-preview dialog that filters `getAvailableInstitutions()` to `csv_import_enabled === true`, auto-selects a sole broker, seeds each row's currency from the discovered currency, and enforces a `.csv` extension and 10 MB cap client-side; `update-account-csv-modal.svelte` is a single-step, single-account dialog with the same file validation.

The institution seam surfaces to the frontend through `GET /api/v1/integration/institutions`, which returns every institution whose `integration_enabled` is true along with its `csv_import_enabled` and `csv_format`; the import modal filters that list itself, so enabling CSV on another broker row makes it selectable without frontend changes. The same `csv_format` specification is repeated verbatim in the docstrings of `src/account/api_types.py`, `src/account/model.py`, `src/account/schema.py` and `src/commands/seed.py`.

`_seed_institutions` seeds only the `WEALTHSIMPLE` institution with `integration_enabled`, `csv_import_enabled` and `csv_format=WEALTHSIMPLE_CSV_FORMAT`, and for an already-existing row it re-asserts `integration_enabled = True`, `is_active = True`, `csv_import_enabled = True` and the template on every run — the mechanism by which a template change reaches an existing database. `seed_data()` always runs the account-type and institution seeds and gates the dev fixtures on `settings.environment == "dev"`.

`tests/conftest.py` sets `STUB_EXTERNAL_API=true` and installs the `seed_reference_data` fixture, which inserts the four `AccountTypeModel` rows and the `WEALTHSIMPLE` `InstitutionModel` with `csv_import_enabled=True` and `csv_format=WEALTHSIMPLE_CSV_FORMAT` for router tests; the global autouse `global_mocks` fixture forces Huey into immediate mode and patches the Redis-backed worker dashboard so no test needs a Redis server.
